paper_id: Aligning Translation-Specific Understanding to General Understanding in Large Language Models__oa_W4404782829
title: Aligning Translation-Specific Understanding to General Understanding in Large Language Models
motivation: LLMs accurately understand concepts in general QA but mistranslate the same concepts literally, revealing internal misalignment
problem_framing: Define translation failure caused by misalignment between translation-specific and general understanding as generalization failure
key_insight: Difficult words are the bottleneck; explicitly extracting interpretations via LLM's general understanding and feeding back to guide translation aligns both understandings
method_signature: DUAT: detect difficult words via draft+QE, generate cross-lingual interpretations, filter via interpretation quality control
evaluation_criteria: COMET/BLEURT scores, human-annotated generalization failures and literalness ratings
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: DUAT increases latency due to multiple prompts; LLMs still fail on neologisms requiring extrinsic knowledge; difficult word detection remains an open question
evidence_for_taste: Difficult words are the bottleneck in translating complex sentences
CoT makes LLMs imitate junior translators rather than advanced translators
DUAT works like senior translators to analyze the complicate words
it is the difficult words that lead to the performance bottleneck
Increasing the number of interpretations does not necessarily lead to performance improvements
thinking_moves: Identifies an internal inconsistency within the same model between different task contexts
Diagnoses the specific locus of failure rather than treating translation holistically
Frames solution as bridging two internal representations (translation-specific vs general)
Uses external tool (QE) to make intrinsic limitation (LLM self-knowledge failure) tractable
Translates abstract understanding alignment into concrete pipeline of detect-interpret-refine
